principles: Criticality is semantic-impact based, not token-type based.
A deterministic token can have semantically uncertain ownership.
Uncertainty in a critical decision dependency blocks automatic PASS.
Non-material uncertainty may coexist with PASS only when explicitly outside every decision dependency.

CRITICAL.definition: A wrong, missing, rebound, or invented value can materially change the scientific proposition, reproducibility, attribution, or protected transaction.
default_examples: subject/object identity when claim meaning depends on them
reproducibility anchors such as seed/iterations when present

MATERIAL.definition: Can affect interpretation or verification but is not automatically critical in every assertion; context-specific escalation is required.

NON_MATERIAL.definition: Stylistic or representational variation proven not to affect scientific meaning or protected dependencies.

escalation_rules.if: field participates in any critical relation edge
anchor has multiple plausible owners and ownership changes scientific meaning
source span is scientifically claim-bearing but unrepresented
escalation_rules.then: CRITICAL unless human/reference rule marks it non-material

escalation_rules.if: candidate adds a scientifically assertive relation with no source alignment
uncertainty concerns only style/format and has no path to a critical assertion

relation_level_criticality.PRECEDES: CRITICAL when source procedure order is explicit and scientifically/reproducibly material
relation_level_criticality.DEPENDS_ON: CRITICAL when dependency affects method meaning or reproducibility
relation_level_criticality.UNCHANGED_DURING: CRITICAL when constancy is part of interpretation/reproducibility
relation_level_criticality.CITES: CRITICAL when citation attribution supports a scientific claim
relation_level_criticality.HAS_VALUE: CRITICAL when quantitative claim meaning depends on it
relation_level_criticality.HAS_UNIT: CRITICAL when quantitative claim meaning depends on it

representation_consistency.frame_role: local assertion semantics and extracted slots
representation_consistency.graph_role: explicit ownership, dependency, and cross-assertion/context relations
rules: If the same critical fact is represented in both frame slots and graph relations, the normalized meanings must agree.
Graph edges may add explicit ownership/dependency structure but may not silently contradict frame slots.
A critical frame-graph disagreement is INVALID_VERIFICATION, not a tie resolved by confidence or semantic voting.
Derived convenience fields must retain a normalization trace to their canonical evidence.
Deterministic anchors are inventoried at top level before assertion ownership is assigned.
Anchor presence/span can be deterministic while ownership remains semantic.
Ownership is expressed by graph relations; assertion anchor_refs are convenience references only.
Unowned critical anchors must be surfaced by coverage checks and cannot silently disappear.
